utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard a lot of noise, but I don't hear my own voice. I was plugged in, in the wrong way. Again, good morning. Before we start, Mr. Russo, I see your present. There was a request by the Defence to make submissions on expert reports and new attachments and new addenda to these reports. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As the Court is aware, in our motion for leave to reply to the Prosecution submission on the Theunens addendum, we believe that leave should have been sought for that addendum. In between our motion for leave and the filing of the Konings addendum, I had sent an e-mail to the Chamber and to the parties, saying that I believe that what was taking place was that if the Chamber did not -- that I had asked the Chamber to instruct the Prosecution not to file any additional addenda without seeking leave until the matter of the Theunens addendum had been resolved. Despite that e-mail, the Prosecution, nevertheless, filed the Konings addendum without seeking leave, and, Your Honour, that is why I would ask for this opportunity to address the Chamber. We have not, obviously, been granted leave to reply to the Prosecution's submission earlier on Theunens. So it seems that the Prosecution's position, based on their response on Theunens, is that no order was issued by the Trial Chamber under Rule 94 and, therefore, their disclosures of expert reports prior to trial were simply self-imposed deadlines which were of a character that was simply of the Prosecution's own goodwill in disclosing addenda. I believe that seriously mischaracterizes the record. I would like to show via Sanction an e-mail that was sent by Chambers sent to Mr. Tieger from the Prosecutor's office. It was sent 19th of December, 2007. I will show it on Sanction now. This is an e-mail that was sent on the 19th of December by Mr. Pittman. It says: "Dear Alan, at the last Status Conference, there was a discussion concerning the filing of the Prosecution expert reports, including that of Reynaud Theunens which was to be filed by 14 December." It cites the transcript. "The Trial Chamber notes that the report has not yet been filed and that no reasons have been given for the delay."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, if I could just interpose an objection, just very quickly, I the Court will rule on it, Your Honour. It was my understanding that the Defence wanted to address the issue of the Konings addendum and not use this as an opportunity to argue the Reynaud addendum, which the Court did not grant leave to reply to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, there is so much related, Mr. Russo, that it would be a bit artificial just to give up one of them, because the issue appears to be the same in respect of both reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It concludes: "The Trial Chamber would, therefore, like an update at your earliest convenience." Now, from Mr. Pittman's e-mail, I believe it is it clear that Judge Moloto, as the Pre-Trial Judge -- actually, I believe, Your Honour, by that point, if I'm not mistaken, I believe Your Honour was already made the Pre-Trial Judge at that time. So, Your Honour, this is actually -- is that right? It is roughly around the same time-period, I could be mistaken, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was approximately at that time that I took over from Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is clear from the record that the discussion concerning the filing of expert reports was with the other Judge Moloto. Whether this e-mail was sent when Your Honour was the Presiding Judge or the Pre-Trial Judge or Judge Moloto, I'm not exactly certain at the moment, but it's roughly the same time-period. In any event, Chambers are Chambers, Chambers clearly understood that these were not some sort of good will deadlines given by the Prosecution. There was, as Your Honour will recall from prior argument concerning the Rule 54 business motion to Croatia, extensive discussion in the 2007 at both 65 ter conferences and at Status Conference about the Defence's desire and the Trial Chamber's desire to ensure that the Prosecution's expert reports were filed in a timely manner before trial. There is no conceivable reason, given the state of the record, given what believe is the clear position of the Trial Chamber in December 2007, that the Prosecution should be allowed now to file, under the guise that they are just addenda, what is -- what amounts to, at least certainly in the case of Konings, a second separate report. Mr. Konings is not in any way clarifying his initial report. He is now submitted a second report which very much addresses particular issues, including targets, target selection, et cetera, which were not part of, in any substantial way, a part of his initial report. This was a second report. I believe the Trial Chamber hats been on notice for several months that the Defence would -- has strongly objected and would continue to strongly object to new reports from experts. This is a question of fairness for the Defence, Your Honours. There has been no motion for leave sought by the Prosecution, so we have no understanding from the Prosecution as to why this couldn't have been done prior to trial, as had been agreed. As I understand it, the documents used for the report, almost of all of them were not only in the possession of OTP but in the position of the expert prior to the time that he rendered his -- his expert report. That certainly goes for Konings. I believe, with respect to Theunens, the documents, many of them, were in OTP's possession. So this, again, leaves us in the position of the OTP avoiding what was clearly discussed at the Rule 54 bis hearing, which was an explanation the Prosecution as to why this wasn't done prior to trial. The practical effect of this is, in terms of fairness, is we now have a new report from Konings that was given to us 32 days before he is scheduled to testify... I'll slow down for the interpreters and court reporters, Your Honours. ... 32 days before he is scheduled to testify. The Court itself can make the clarification, but I believe at least half of the witnesses, if not more, that have appeared have talked about shelling. We now have a report where the opportunity to put matters in Mr. Konings' report to witnesses of the Prosecution is now been lost. There, of course, may be issues that overlap and that were covered, but, nevertheless, there are other issues in his report that cannot be put to witnesses that the Prosecution has called that contradict some of the findings in Mr. Konings's report. We've lost that opportunity. Just as importantly, the Prosecution doesn't explain why that opportunity was lost, doesn't explain why this report wasn't filed in a timely manner prior to trial. So, Your Honours, my position is that we have substantial reasons to discuss and address with the Trial Chamber whether these addenda are admissible. We believe that the first step is to require the Prosecution to seek leave. Rule 94 bis (A) is, I believe, clear and I see no reason why the Prosecution should be allowed to take the position that, as long as this trial is going on, they can just submit expert reports to us whenever they please. That's apparently their position now because they say there was never an order, there was never an obligation to provide the report in the first place. So, in theory, and, ultimately, this is it my main concern, Your Honour, we have a Rule 54 bis motion which the Republic of Croatia responded to, but the Chamber still, I believe, based on its September order, still has to review the order and will make further determinations on that Rule 54 bis request. Given now that they filed a second Konings addendum, what is the -- what is it going happen with the Rule 54 bis proceeding? What happens -- are we to expect now that there is a possibility that there will a third addendum because they're also pursuing additional documents from the Republic of Croatia on artillery? When does it end? I mean, our position is, Your Honour, that there are substantial issues here, there is a threat of more addenda if the Trial Chamber does not intervene, and we believe that there is no reason procedurally why the Prosecution should be allowed to avoid having to disclose to the Trial Chamber at least its reasons for doing this at this late stage. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One -- two points I'd like to add. One is: We still have yet to receive a translation of this report or a response to the request for when a translation would be forthcoming. The second is: This is an example of conforming expert reports to the Defences that have been coming into the case throughout the case. We get a report, we're supposed to respond to it, or -- that's the Prosecution's burden to give us this report to tell us what their experts's theories are. What's happened here is, through cross-examination, various Defences have been put forth. That has changed because of -- from the Prosecution's standpoint, because now other things that the Defence has addressed have not been addressed by their experts. Then all of a sudden, in mid stream now, they want to submit reports to the us that are -- try to conform to some of the Defences that have been put forth in the case. It is simply not a proper way of producing an expert report under Rule 94, so we are prejudiced twice in this particular instances. That's all I wanted to add Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have nothing to add because the supplementals do not affect the case of Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours, it is only my intention to address the Konings addendum, unless the Court would like to hear argument also with respect to the addendum of Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said that it was artificial to separate them completely, that, of course, gives an opportunity for you to respond to what has been said by Mr. Misetic in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The reason I interposed an objection is because I believe that the Konings addendum is, in fact, not the same issue as the addendum of Mr. Theunens, for a very simple reason, that the court has already issued a ruling on this issue with respect to Lieutenant-Colonel Konings' report. If the Chamber will recall, the Defence filed a motion in limine, under Rule, seeking to preclude Lieutenant-Colonel Konings from offering the testimony which is in his addendum report, specifically testifying with respect to whether targets selected or hit were legitimate military targets. I believe it was on the 21st of May of this year that the Court issued its ruling with respect to that. The context of this was that after the Lieutenant-Colonel Konings filed his initial report, the Defence filed their Rule 73 motion, seeking to preclude that testimony, because they said his report was not Knin specific and, therefore, this testimony should not be aloud because it was not specifically addressed in the original report. The Court issued the rules denying that motion, and I will quote the Court at paragraph 7 of that decision, and it very clearly indicates: "The Prosecution is obliged to give notice of evidence that it intends to present through proper disclosure. If proper notice has been given, a party may examine an expert witness with respect to matters not included in his or her expert report, so long as they are within the knowledge of the witness, relevant, and probative." Now, it's the Prosecution's position that it was entitled to ask these questions of Lieutenant-Colonel Konings on the stand without having filed an addendum report. The only issue would be notice to the Defence of what Lieutenant-Colonel Konings would testify to if asked those questions. Now, Rule 94 bis is the only procedural mechanism by which the -- the Prosecution can provide normal to the Defence of what those answers will be. So the Konings report is distinct from the Theunens report in that respect because the Court has specifically issued a ruling on this very issue. It would be a bit in opposite if the Court had already given the Prosecution permission to ask these questions through proper disclosure and then to force the Prosecution to seek leave in order to provide that disclosure. So this was the only mechanism available to us to do so. If the Court pleases, I'm happy to address the issue of Mr. Theunens as well, because the Defence`s position that for some reason they are prejudiced by this late disclosure of issues is not necessarily accurate, especially given the fact that the Theunens report clearly indicates that it is based on documentation received subsequent to the filing of the original report. The issue is one of practicality from the Prosecution's perspective. We have every right to issue addendums to these reports to the extent they address knew information received in the ongoing investigation. Of course, the Court has not issued a rules with respect to the Prosecution's 54 bis application; however, if additional documentation is it forthcoming as a result of that application, the Prosecution has an obligation to disclose that to the Defence and to present that evidence to the Trial Chamber if it is relevant and probative to the issues before the Chamber. That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I can just address the issue of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- the 21 May - excuse me - the 21 May order that Mr. Russo references. It talks about proper disclosure. Now, I believe that there's nothing inconsistent between what we said in that order, which is, what is proper disclosure of an expert's opinions. If it is an expert report, which is what this is, and it was disclosed under Rule 894, which is what they did, then the proper way to do this would have been to file a motion for leave with the Trial Chamber to file an additional report. Now, whether the Trial Chamber then would have granted or would not have granted leave is up to, of course, the Trial Chamber, but it gives the parties the opportunity to address the matter. So, Your Honour, again, I state that if it were the interpretation of Mr. Russo, in essence, what it means is that in ICTY proceedings, the Prosecution can file a three-page expert report, and within 30 days of that expert's testimony, file 100 pages on the Defence and say, "This is just disclosure of some additional questions we're going to be asking him." I don't think that the procedural fairness that is guaranteed by this Tribunal would support such practice, and I, therefore, believe that seeking leave is not inconsistent with the notion of proper disclosure as discussed by the Trial Chamber in its order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other Defence counsel wish to add anything? Mr. Russo, another minute for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe it is bit unfair to characterize the situation as the Defence has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has noticed that the addendum is not 30 times the size of the original. There is no need to expound on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further? Then the Chamber will consider the matter and we'll give our decision. Then we move on. For your next witness, Mr. Russo, there's an application -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Witness 84 and there is an application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts, as a matter of fact, since the suggestion was that if the application would be granted, that the more or less logical consequence would be that we would hear the evidence of this witness in closed session, rather than in the situation of face distortion, voice distortion. So, therefore, I suggest that we also hear and give an opportunity to put further questions to this witness in relation to the protective measures in closed session. We move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I just wanted to put on the record something in light of the fact that the -- Mr. Russo, for the first time, raised the 21 May 2008 decision of the Trial Chamber this morning. In reviewing that quickly, I wanted to make a couple of points. First, I did research it, Your Honour, and concerning Mr. Pittman's e-mail of the 19th of December, you appointed yourself the Pre-Trial Judge on the 11th of December. So at the time of that e-mail, you, in fact, were the Pre-Trial Judge. The second issue is that -- the second issue is that we wish to alert the Trial Chamber to the jurisprudence of Trial Chamber I, the decision which was issued last week on a matter which I believe is quite similar to the one pending before the Chamber. It is the decision of Trial Chamber I, dated 27 October 2008, decision on Defence motions to exclude the expert reports of Mr. Patrick J. Treanor. I call the Trial Chamber's attention to paragraphs 15 and 16, in which the Trial Chamber there - and the Chamber can read it - but in which the Chamber found that the Prosecution's failure to show good cause as to why it was filing a second report after the deadline for filing of Prosecution expert reports had passed, and that, as a result of that failure, that would be a reason to strike that -- that second report. This, I believe, is consistent with the position we're taking here, that the Prosecution must show good cause as to why it is filing these reports at this hour of the proceeding, and that is our submission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence is, first of all, conflating the arguments that the Prosecution has made with respect to the Konings and the Theunens addendums. I don't know why the Defence is characterizing the Prosecution's position regarding Rule 73 discussion of this Chamber as being raised for the first time. The Rule 73 ruling only applies to the addendum report of Lieutenant-Colonel Konings, and this is the first time that we have addressed that issue. The Prosecution is not taking the position that the Rule 73 ruling by this Court affects the admissibility of Mr. Theunens's addendum. The Perisic decision obviously has no effect on the Prosecution's argument with respect to Konings addendum, as that is related entirely to the 21st May decision by this Court. If you want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that what you wanted to say, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I thought he was going to interpose an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: With respect to the Perisic decision, Your Honour, insforas it relates to the Theunens' report, I would note, first of all, that the decision is in opposite to this case, for the very clear reason in the same paragraph that -- the same paragraphs that Mr. Misetic mentions, that decision was based, as that Trial Chamber noted, on the fact that the second report of Patrick Treanor was based entirely on documents available to the Prosecution since June of 2005, prior to the filing of the first report. As we've already indicated, Mr. Theunens' report is based on evidence which the Prosecution has received subsequent to the filing of his first report. For that reason, the decision is not applicable; and in any case, it is also based on the Trial Chamber's notation that the Prosecution did not show any good cause for why the report was filed later. In this case, Your Honours, Mr. Theunens in his addendum report provided that good cause in the introduction, by indicating that it was based only on documentation received after the filing of the first report. So, in any case, with respect to the Konings' report, even if the Perisic decision applied, which we -- our position is that it does not, this Chamber had already issued a binding decision on the parties with respect to the filing of information with respect to Lieutenant-Colonel Konings. We were bound do apply it. I'm sure the Defence is not taking the position that if Trial Chamber -- the Perisic Trial Chamber had ruled differently from this Trial Chamber, that we would be obliged to follow that Trial Chamber, as opposed to ruling by this Chamber, on the exact same issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all Trial Chamber wanted. That helps us outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may briefly respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic. Could you try to do that in one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First point is that the May 2 is decision is a decision to not in limine bar them from filing a second report. It is not a decision on merits here as to whether they need to file or seek leave. Secondly, I think the jurisprudence should be consistent in terms of whether or not the Prosecution has an obligation to show good cause when it seeks to admit reports after the deadline has passed. I believe there is nothing -- there should be nothing controversial about that decision. Third, the very reason why we asked that they have to seek life is Mr. Russo, who in discussing Mr. Theunens, I believe the fact is that these are documents were in OTP's possession, but not in Mr. Theunens' possession, in which case if that's the case, we're talking about an OTP employee who didn't receive documents that are in OTP's possession. And, finally, I'm not conflating the two issues. This is a -- I don't see any reason why an artillery expert should be -- have different set of rules and a different set of jurisprudence than any other expert. The rules for an expert witness should be the same regardless of the subject matter about which the expert is testifying. I believe those rules should be consistent between Chambers. And, finally, Your Honour, just so that the Court is aware of procedural what we are doing here, in light of Trial Chamber I's decision last week, we are, in fact, preparing a motion to strike the Theunens's reports in their entirety. So what we're dealing with here is the issue of Konings and the filing of the addendum in the Konings matter. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Russo, another 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I will be brief. The Prosecution is not arguing for a different standard to be applied between the Konings and the Theunens report, the Prosecution's position is that the issue of the Konings report has already been litigated and decided upon by the Trial Chamber. With respect to motions to strike, Your Honour, I would ask the Court -- this is already a subject of filings before the Court, the Defence asked to argue the Konings issue orally. I don't -- I would ask the Court to issue an order that there no further written submission with respect to either the Theunens or the Konings report, insforas those have already been brought to the attention of the Chamber and argued by the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will further consider the matter. We were informed, first of all, that we have to return into open session. I failed to do so, and our discussion on the procedural matter after the witness left --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- after the witness left the courtroom, I think that this discussion should be public discussion, nothing else. So, therefore, Mr. Registrar, if you would take the appropriate action to have this part of the transcript being made public. Mr. Cermak, the Chamber was informed that you are suffering, like many people these days, from the flu. If this would ever cause you any problem in following the proceedings, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your concern, but I can endure without any problems. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cermak. We will adjourn and resume on Wednesday, the 5th of November, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Closed session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
